title: Monteverde diagnostics onramp scratchbook
body:
Call date: 2025-11-13
Participants: Priya (Redwood SE), Ethan (Redwood TPM), Dr. Luis Ramos (Monteverde CTO), Sara Kim (Monteverde ML), Legal: N/A on call

High-level ask
- Monteverde wants an assistant that ingests diagnostic imaging reports + clinical notes and returns a concise clinician-facing summary + structured flags (e.g., critical lab out of range, urgent follow-up recommended).
- Priority: data residency and PHI controls (HIPAA), predictable latency for point-of-care (<250ms tail for short summaries), and fail-safe on hallucinations.
- Target go-live: pilot in Q2 2026 (internal clinicians, ~20 users).

Functional requirements (from call)
- Input sources: HL7-ish JSON, PDF text extraction (they will pre-extract), and free-text clinician notes.
- Output: short 2–4 line actionable summary + JSON with fields: urgency_level (low/medium/high), critical_finding_tags (list), recommended_action_codes (list), confidence_score (0.0-1.0).
- Audit trail: want token-level request/response logging (redacted PHI) and signed request IDs for traceability.
- Model explainability: show provenance sentences (sentence-level pointers) for any critical flag.

Non-functional requirements
- Security: must support VPC private deployment or on-prem package, customer-managed KMS, and audited access logs.
- Residency: initial pilot in US-East; eventual EU region for EU trials.
- Latency: P50 target 120ms; P95 < 250ms for single-document summarization when average input token length ~600 tokens.
- Throughput: pilot QPS expected 3 sustained, burst to 20. Prod estimate (if successful): 25 sustained, 200 bursts.
- Cost sensitivity: wants guidance to reduce per-token cost; will consider quantized models if accuracy acceptable.

Constraints / gotchas noted on call
- Data format variability: their notes often include copy-pasted templates with lots of boilerplate. Need robust prefix/trimming to avoid repeated context.
- Hallucination risk: clinical domain — even low-frequency hallucinations are unacceptable. They insisted on conservative defaults (prefer false negatives over false positives for urgent flags).
- PDF extraction fidelity: images embedded with OCR errors create weird tokens — front-line pipeline must include simple OCR QC heuristics (digit ratio, improbable character runs).
- Token budget per request unclear — Sara said average clinician note is ~1,200 chars but can spike. We need distribution.

Immediate technical observations (SE quick take)
- Best path: Redwood Private (VPC) during pilot to address HIPAA and KMS. Recommend dedicated node pool (small) with autocaling for bursts.
- Model choice: evaluate two families: closed-domain clinical fine-tuned LLM (if available) and a robust open model (e.g., med-7b-quant) as fallback. Start with 7B quantized variants to meet latency and cost.
- Caching: implement prefix/KV caching for repeated boilerplate. For this workload, caching should reduce token compute by ~20–35% (estimate).
- Safety layer: add post-hoc deterministic checks (regex and medical-rule heuristics) to suppress hallucinated medication recommendations or impossible vitals.
- Explainability: use model with token-aligned attention or generate provenance by asking model to emit annotated spans; then map spans back to source sentences for audit.

Evaluation plan (proposal)
- Build 200-item prompt/eval set from Monteverde historical deidentified notes (they can ship a redacted sample). Split: 140 train/dev, 60 held-out for hallucination and recall checks.
- Metrics: Precision/Recall/F1 for critical flags, hallucination rate (binary), and clinician satisfaction (Likert 1–5) from small usability study.
- Thresholding policy: set conservative cutoff for urgent flags (target recall 0.92, precision >0.85) — adjust after first 30 clinician sessions.

Sample prompt (working)
- System: "You are a concise clinical summarizer. Output two sections: SUMMARY (2–4 lines) and STRUCTURED JSON with keys urgency_level, critical_finding_tags, recommended_action_codes, confidence_score, provenance_sentences (list). Do not invent facts. If insufficient evidence, set urgency_level to low and confidence_score to <0.5 and explain uncertainty in SUMMARY."
- User input: [raw extracted text]
- Post-process: run deterministic checks (med list cross-check, impossible labs) and if post-check fails, add note: "FLAGGED_FOR_REVIEW: deterministic check"

Open questions / items to clarify with Monteverde
- Will they provide a deidentified corpus for model eval, and what's the exact token length distribution? (Action: Ethan to request a sample dump, due 2025-11-20)
- What legal review timeline for PHI handling in pilot? (Action: Priya to loop in Redwood legal; Monteverde legal TBD)
- Acceptance criteria for pilot (what % clinician adoption/accuracy considered successful?) — need Monteverde product input.
- Are there specific KMS/HSM providers required? (they mentioned AWS KMS initially; confirm)

Immediate next steps (owners and rough ETA)
- Ethan: request 200 deidentified notes sample + token distribution CSV from Monteverde (ETA: 2025-11-20).
- Priya: prepare draft Redwood Private architecture diagram with KMS/HSM integration and minimal SLOs (ETA: 2025-11-24).
- Maya: spin up small benchmark harness for med-7b-quant vs med-13b (quant) locally, baseline latency and ROUGE-like summary metrics (ETA: 2025-11-28).
- Monteverde (Sara): confirm redaction process and legal contact (ETA: 2025-11-18).

Risks & mitigation
- Risk: Hallucination in clinical outputs -> Mitigation: conservative inference, deterministic post-checks, clinician-in-loop confirmation UI.
- Risk: Unexpected spikes in token length -> Mitigation: truncate + summarize long history into compressed context (use retrieval or two-stage summarization).
- Risk: Compliance delays -> Mitigation: run parallel low-risk PoC on synthetic or fully deidentified data to validate flow while legal finalizes.

Notes to self (Priya)
- Bring up canary rollback: configure automatic fallback to simpler heuristics if model returns low confidence.
- Think about per-route cost visibility for Monteverde finance team — show sample per-summary cost with different quantization profiles.
- Add one-slide tradeoff: accuracy vs latency vs cost (7b quant vs 13b fp16) for next meeting.

Meeting artifacts to attach later
- Architecture diagram (Redwood Private VPC + KMS), benchmark table, eval plan (200 items)

Status: draft. Keep this as the working scratchbook until Monteverde confirms data share and we run first benchmarks.

-- end of scratchbook (quick capture)
